_note: The UNIFIED route-table resolution rule (/web/04-routing.md): given a routes.json table and a concrete path, which entry matches and what does the screen receive? Pins the grammar every renderer consumes from the SAME file — `component` (the native screen / web component this path mounts), vars = matched params + parsed query MERGED WITH QUERY WINNING (the web navigatePath `{ ...params, ...query }` rule), and `meta.title` (the declared title: web sets document.title, native seeds the system bar with it when the component's own claim is unknown). First match wins, DSXPathMatch grammar ({name} / :name / *), unconditional `redirect` entries follow before matching completes (depth-capped in the runtimes). `component: null` = no component route matched — each runtime's degrade is its own documented business (web warns + no-ops; native falls to the configured web fallback, deriving a bar title for PUSHED frames — native-only behavior pinned by RouterTest, not here). Executors: Kotlin RouterTest.resolveMatchesTheSharedConformanceCorpus (END-TO-END: seeds the table, pushes, asserts the frame + seeded chrome); TS packages/dom/test/router.test.ts (drives the real FrameRouter.resolveUrl + the navigatePath vars rule); Swift Engine/iOS/Router.swift resolved()/materialize() is the compile-pending REFERENCE.

cases.name: an exact path mounts its component, no vars, no declared title
brace params and query both land in vars; meta.title is the declared title
first match wins — table order is precedence
colon params are the same grammar as braces
an unconditional redirect entry resolves through to its target
a trailing star soaks the rest of the path (no params)
no component route matched — each runtime degrades its own documented way
